doc.title: John LaPorta interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, Florida, April 13, 1996

title: Moving to Berklee
summary: After ten years teaching privately in New York he met Bob Share, was sent to Berklee, and found about 100 of 140 students needing attention.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: But then you ended up at Berklee.

Well I taught privately, and in New York City for ten years or so. And I really wanted to make a move. I thought my musical life was starting to diminish there. I had the family and I was busy raising them and it seemed like everything I was doing took more and more energy to do and I wanted to get into a different area. So I had started I think the summer camps had been going on for about two years and I decided to sound around about getting into some kind of college teaching and I met Bob Share then, who was provost for Berklee School of Music then. I talked to him about it and he was the first one I ever did, and he said, “Why don’t you come up to Boston and meet Marty Berk, I think he’d like to talk to you.” So that’s the way that happened.
When you started at Berklee, how large a school was it?

Well we had about 140 students. And I noticed a hundred of them were milling around wondering what to do. There were about 40 of them getting really taken care of by Herb Pomeroy and those people, and then these other people weren’t quite so good. I figured well this is the area I need to address. And the school I think has somewhere in the area of 2700 students, but it’s much broader now. There are all kinds of majors there and so forth. In fact they just recently started getting into a Master’s program there, in the last two years.
